title: Choose class, struct or record semantics from identity, equality, copying and inheritance requirements

questions.prompt: Explain what ordinary assignment (`b = a`) copies for a C# `record class` and for a `record struct`.

rubric.point: Record-class assignment copies a reference, so both variables refer to the same instance.
Record-struct assignment copies the value's fields into separate storage; this is a shallow value copy, not a deep copy of referenced objects.

questions.model: A record class copies a reference to the same instance. A record struct copies its fields into a separate value; any reference fields still point to the same objects.

questions.prompt: A C# message model needs generated value equality and a base type from which specialised message types inherit. Both `record class` and `readonly record struct` generate value equality. Why does the inheritance requirement favour `record class`?

rubric.point: Record classes support inheritance by derived record classes, whereas record structs cannot serve as inheritable base types.

questions.model: A record class can be a base for derived record classes. A record struct cannot be inherited from.
